title: Create the devcontainer and reproducible development toolchain
why: A consistent environment lets you and Astra reproduce the same install, database connection, lint results, and debugging behavior across Windows/WSL and Linux.
what: Create a devcontainer with Python, Node, Git, PostgreSQL client tools, and a non-root development user.
Define a development Compose setup and documented task commands; keep production configuration separate.
how: Use a supported Python release and Node LTS; pin the chosen versions and lock dependency resolutions. Record selections in docs/development.md.
Configure .devcontainer/devcontainer.json, a development Dockerfile, and a PostgreSQL service with a named volume and healthcheck. Forward only development ports.
Install dependencies through uv and the selected JavaScript package manager. Add Python/TypeScript formatting, linting, and editor debug configurations.
Provide placeholder environment variables and an explicit setup command. Do not put API keys or personal watchlists in images, tracked files, or lifecycle-hook output.
done: A clean clone opens in the devcontainer and the non-root user can edit files.
Python, Node, package managers, and PostgreSQL client versions are documented and reproducible.
The database healthcheck succeeds and survives a container restart.
Setup commands succeed without paid credentials; provider-dependent commands report what is missing.
Documented Windows/WSL and Linux startup instructions contain no unimplemented success claims.

title: Qualify the Solana data source and capture representative fixtures
why: First-live estimates depend on a feed that actually covers the watched wallets, supported swap routes, and reconnect recovery. Writing the UI before proving this can leave a convincing but unusable application.
what: Evaluate one primary Solana provider and its decoded stream plus historical lookup capabilities.
Define the supported execution types, coverage limits, rate/credit budget, and recovery strategy before implementing the collector.
how: Start with Helius Parsed Streams and its current official documentation; verify account filtering, supported programs, credentials, and confirmation fields against real payloads. Treat decoded instructions as inputs, not automatic proof of a buy.
Use a small user-supplied wallet list. Capture sanitized examples of a buy, sell, ordinary transfer, failed transaction, multi-leg swap, wrapped SOL flow, duplicate delivery, and unsupported route.
Prove how to recover events after disconnects. If the stream lacks replay, qualify a history endpoint and a bounded overlap/backfill strategy.
Measure delivery delay and credit usage for an explicitly recorded sample interval. Document unavailable FOMO-specific fields separately; do not use Wind endpoints as the backend.
done: docs/data-source-contract.md names the chosen feed, credential mechanism, supported programs, commitment, rate limits, costs, and failure responses.
Every fixture has provenance and an expected classification, including unknown cases.
A documented disconnect experiment identifies the available recovery path and its coverage limits.
No credential, private watchlist, or unsolicited personal identity information is committed.
A go/no-go decision permits the wallet-first path or lists the exact blocked capability.

title: Bootstrap the API, worker, frontend, and configuration contract
why: One codebase with explicit service boundaries keeps a personal deployment manageable while allowing collection to run independently of browser requests.
what: Create a Python backend package with API and worker entrypoints, plus a React/TypeScript frontend.
Define typed settings, health endpoints, structured logs, dependency locks, and a local development command surface.
how: Use FastAPI for HTTP/WebSocket, an asynchronous worker process, and a conventional React build. Avoid microservices or a mandatory Redis dependency.
Validate configuration on startup. Distinguish required database configuration from optional provider/Telegram credentials and enabled feature flags.
Provide liveness and readiness endpoints; readiness should reflect the service's actual dependencies. Serve a minimal frontend with explicit empty and offline states.
Keep any commands added to README executable. Provide a fixture mode so ordinary development and CI do not require external API calls.
done: API, worker, and frontend start using the documented commands.
Invalid settings fail with useful, redacted errors.
Fixture mode runs without provider or Telegram credentials.
Logs contain service/event identifiers but no secret values or credential-bearing URLs.
Pinned dependency files and a concise directory map are committed.

title: Implement PostgreSQL migrations, canonical identities, and durable jobs
why: Stable identities and transactional persistence prevent duplicated trades, mismatched tokens, and lost work when the collector or API restarts.
what: Create the initial relational schema and migrations for watches, identities, source records, events, executions, quotes, checkpoints, jobs, and notifications.
Define uniqueness constraints, precision, event revisions, and a committed delivery sequence.
how: Use chain plus canonical address for wallets/tokens; preserve Solana case. Separate human labels from evidence-bearing account-wallet links.
Deduplicate raw source IDs and economic executions with chain/signature/instruction identity where available. Store raw payloads with bounded retention.
Use integer/high-precision numeric quantities and decimal values; store UTC timestamps and explicit unknown/missing states.

Write canonical mutations and an outbox row in the same transaction. A single ordered dispatcher must assign/persist a committed delivery sequence; do not use a pre-commit sequence as the replay watermark.
Implement migrations and indexed access paths. Keep jobs claimable with a lease and bounded retries; one process may still crash mid-job.
done: Migrations apply to an empty database and an upgrade path is documented.
Duplicate fixture ingestion does not create extra executions.
Two distinct same-amount swaps remain distinct.
A rollback does not advance the safe source checkpoint or emit a phantom committed event.
Precision, address case, and chain separation survive a database round-trip.
No user, billing, entitlement, quota, or session tables are introduced.

title: Implement personal watchlists, aliases, groups, and bulk import
why: The collector needs one unambiguous watch scope, and you need to adjust it without editing source code or creating a product account.
what: Provide add/list/edit/pause/remove operations for wallet watches, notes, aliases, and groups.
Add a small bulk import/export contract with per-row validation and an explicit initial list of 10–25 wallets.
how: Validate addresses by chain and reject malformed inputs without case-folding Solana addresses.
Separate removing a watch from deleting its historical records. Record monitoring states such as resolving, active, paused, unsupported, and error.
Make repeated additions idempotent. Preview imports and return valid, duplicate, and invalid rows without silent partial success.
Store manual identity labels as manual. Use group membership for filters and later signals; do not call a wallet label a verified person.
done: Single and bulk operations work through the API with clear error responses.
Duplicate entries do not create duplicate source subscriptions.
Pausing a watch changes collection/subscription intent while preserving history.
Group rename/delete behavior is specified and covered by representative integration checks.
No login, commercial quota, public account directory, or exclusive resource flow is added.

title: Build the provider adapter and live collection worker
why: Always-on ingestion is the source of the live feed. The browser must not be responsible for keeping collection running.
what: Implement the qualified outbound stream adapter and persist raw source events.
Manage watch-filter changes, reconnect/backoff, bounded processing, and source health.
how: Hide provider payloads behind a small adapter interface: capabilities, subscription updates, event envelope, history lookup, and health.

Prefer the qualified outbound WebSocket path so the private dashboard needs no public webhook endpoint. If an approved provider requires callbacks, expose only a separately authenticated ingestion route.
Persist accepted source records and durable processing work before advancing a safe source checkpoint.
Handle disconnects, subscription rejection, rate limiting, malformed payloads, and provider-schema changes. Quarantine unrecognized payloads instead of discarding them silently.
Bound queues and retries. On watch changes, avoid overlapping subscriptions causing unbounded duplicate delivery.
done: A real qualified wallet produces persisted source events without an open browser.
Duplicate source notifications are harmless.
A restart restores watch intent and initiates gap recovery.
Rate-limit responses trigger backoff and a visible degraded state.
Captured sensitive query parameters are redacted from logs.
No trade-signing, execution, or private-key handling code exists.

title: Normalize swaps and reconcile transaction confirmation
why: A decoded instruction or incoming transfer does not necessarily mean the watched wallet bought a token. Incorrect attribution would contaminate every downstream view and alert.
what: Convert supported source records into canonical economic executions and explicit unknown/unsupported events.
Separate trade execution outcome from chain confirmation and preserve revisions.
how: Attribute balance changes and execution legs to the watched wallet; account for fees, wrapped SOL, token-account creation/rent, and routed swaps.
Merge legs only with sufficient transaction/instruction evidence. Keep two independent orders or swaps separate even if time and amount match.
Use fixture-driven route handlers for programs proved in WO-002. Unsupported routes remain visible with a reason and source link.
Track observed/confirmed/finalized/corrected chain facts without inventing off-chain FOMO order states. Failed transactions cannot contribute to confirmed trade totals.
Apply later status changes idempotently; publish revisions and reverse any now-invalid derived contributions.
done: Representative buy, sell, transfer, failed, routed, and wrapped-SOL fixtures classify correctly.
Amounts retain raw precision and fees are distinguished from acquired/sold quantity.
Transfer-only records do not trigger buy/sell alerts.
Duplicate delivery creates one appropriate execution; distinct swaps are not collapsed.
Confirmation/status corrections are reflected in history with provenance.

title: Implement durable recovery, bounded backfill, and gap reporting
why: A tracker that loses activity whenever the VPS or provider disconnects cannot support dependable histories or signals.
what: Recover missed source activity using persisted checkpoints and the qualified history endpoint.
Separate live delivery from historical replay and expose unrecoverable coverage gaps.
how: Persist a per-source/per-watch recovery boundary supported by the provider. Use an overlap window and stable deduplication rather than assuming a perfect replay cursor.
Process backfill through the same normalization code as live events, tagged with replay provenance and alert eligibility.
Bound backfill depth, page count, concurrency, and credits. Persist job progress and retry leases so interruption is resumable.
Define the source-history limit and record a gap if it prevents complete recovery. Never advance a checkpoint over failed unpersisted work.
Maintain event occurrence order separately from the ordered delivery log; late source events are valid.
done: An outage-and-restart exercise recovers known missing fixtures without duplicates.
Live ingestion can continue while a bounded backfill runs.
Historical imports do not flood Telegram.
A second interruption resumes rather than restarting an unlimited scan.
Coverage gaps are returned by the API and visible to the user.
A database transaction rollback does not falsely move the recovery boundary.

title: Add token metadata, quote caching, and market-data provenance
why: Useful trade cards need decimals, names, and available market context, but stale or missing prices must not become fabricated execution values.
what: Resolve token metadata and cache current quotes for tokens in the watch scope.
Keep execution valuation separate from current market valuation.
how: Use chain/address keys and timestamped provider adapters. Request only observed or opened tokens, with bounded TTL refresh and concurrency.
Retain raw execution quantities; compute historical USD values only from a sufficiently contemporaneous and attributable price source.
Expose price source, observation time, stale/missing state, and available market fields. Do not treat missing market cap or liquidity as zero.
Reject late stale updates overwriting newer quotes. Handle duplicate symbols, multiple pools, decimal corrections, and token-not-found responses.
Batch requests where the provider supports it and surface usage against the configured monthly budget.
done: A newer quote survives a later-arriving older response.
Missing prices remain null and do not enter USD rankings as zero.
Exact chain/address lookup cannot mix tokens with the same ticker.
Price outages leave raw trade quantities and explorer links usable.
Refresh demand remains within documented rate limits in the small-watchlist trial.

title: Build feed, history, wallet/token queries, and search APIs
why: One consistent read contract keeps feed, detail pages, and future analytics aligned and prevents duplicated business rules in the frontend.
what: Expose read APIs for event history, wallets, tokens, source health, and exact/alias search.
Implement cursor pagination and personal filters without entitlement gates.
how: Define response DTOs for event revision, chain, wallet, token, status, quantities, valuation provenance, and coverage.
Use stable composite ordering for history pagination; specify occurrence-time versus delivery-time views and late-event behavior.
Implement wallet/group, token, direction, amount, time-window, and supported-state filters with indexed SQL.
Use exact address/signature lookup before text search. Limit result sizes and return useful invalid-cursor errors.
Document endpoints in generated OpenAPI plus short request/response examples; keep raw credentials and excessive provider payloads out of responses.
done: Initial page and subsequent pages contain no duplicate records for a stable snapshot.
Filters have the same meaning on feed and detail queries.
Missing prices and partial coverage remain explicit in responses.
Queries on the measured pilot dataset meet a recorded latency target.
Address search preserves Solana case and includes chain identity.

title: Implement live updates with a committed replay cursor
why: Network changes and browser suspension must not create missing cards, duplicate rows, or stale event states.
what: Add WebSocket delivery of new events, revisions, source status, and reconnect catch-up.
Use the committed dispatch log as the live cursor and define its retention behavior.
how: Assign delivery positions through one transactionally ordered dispatcher after canonical commits; use the outbox to bridge API/worker failures.
Define hello/cursor, event, event_update, status, heartbeat, resync-required, and error messages with versioned schemas.
Coordinate catch-up and live attachment around a committed watermark. Resume without a race between the history response and live stream.
If a cursor predates retained delivery history, request a bounded resnapshot and show that transition; do not silently claim full recovery.
Bound client buffers and apply backpressure/disconnect behavior. Browser reconnects use jitter and do not retrigger old notifications.
done: Disconnecting while new events arrive restores all retained events once.
An update modifies the existing card identity rather than inserting a duplicate.
Out-of-order source timestamps do not break the delivery cursor.
Expired cursors produce an explicit resync path.
A concurrent-commit regression demonstrates that the watermark cannot skip a later commit with an earlier allocated database ID.

title: Build the responsive live feed and watchlist interface
why: The first release should let you follow activity in one place without the complexity of Wind's commercial workspace.
what: Build fixed Feed, Watchlist, and Settings navigation with responsive trade cards.
Add watch editing, filters, connection/coverage states, and stable reading behavior.
how: Use reusable typed components and a small state layer. Render the API's data rather than recomputing trade semantics in the browser.
Implement a virtualized or otherwise bounded feed, cursor loading, a new-event counter, and jump-to-latest while preserving the user's scroll position.
Support copy wallet/token address, explorer links, group/direction/amount filters, and visible unknown/stale fields.
Provide accessible controls, keyboard focus, mobile-width layouts, and explicit loading, empty, partial, offline, and error states.
Use original styling and assets. No audio, account login, Pro upsell, or drag/resize workspace is required.
done: A real subscribed event appears, updates in place, and remains in history after reload.
Adding/pausing a wallet changes the backend watch state and shows the result.
New events do not repeatedly pull the reader away from older cards.
Core flows work at desktop and approximately 390px mobile width.
No source keys or Telegram token appear in the browser bundle or network responses.

title: Add wallet and token drill-down views
why: An alert becomes useful when you can immediately see the observed wallet/token history and the limits of the available evidence.
what: Build wallet detail and token detail using the shared read contracts.
Show filtered trade history, available quote fields, exact identities, and source links.
how: Add wallet-to-token and token-to-wallet navigation while keeping the selected filters and chain context.
Display observed buy/sell totals only from eligible executions. Show sample start, last update, missing USD values, and coverage gaps.
Use wallet aliases as labels and preserve full addresses. Keep FOMO identity fields absent until their evidence-bearing integration exists.
Load expensive histories incrementally and reuse quote/cache state without silently substituting latest prices for execution prices.
done: Opening a feed event reaches the correct chain/address detail page.
Wallet-token queries agree with the same filtered events in the feed.
Incomplete history is labelled and no complete P&L or platform-wide holdings claim appears.
Empty and unavailable token data produce useful states.
A link can be refreshed or opened directly without losing its identity.

title: Deliver alerts to one Telegram chat with durable retries
why: One outbound channel lets you use the tracker without keeping its dashboard open. Reliability requires more than a direct send inside the collector.
what: Implement one server-configured bot token and destination chat.
Queue eligible new trades for delivery with filtering, retries, deduplication, and stale-event expiry.
how: Write notification intent transactionally and process sends in the worker. Keep bot tokens in server-side secrets and use a manual test-message action.
Define direction, wallet/group, amount, and optional token filters with a versioned rule snapshot. Recheck mutable rules before delayed sends.
Use canonical event ID plus destination as the notification identity; store Telegram message IDs for supported corrections.
Respect retry-after responses and backoff. Distinguish definite failures from uncertain acknowledgment timeouts; document the chosen resend tradeoff.
Suppress historical replay and stale alerts; keep operational delivery errors separate from successful trade events.
done: A qualifying real event reaches the configured chat with token, wallet, amount, time, and explorer link.
Duplicate ingestion does not normally create a second notification.
Rate-limit/transient failures retry without blocking ingestion.
Backfill and database restore do not resend the entire history.
The UI never receives the bot token, and no Bark/audio/multi-customer binding system is introduced.
The runbook explicitly avoids an exactly-once delivery guarantee.

title: Add CI and meaningful fixture-based regression gates
why: Fast AI-assisted iteration needs executable checks for data correctness and recovery, without making every CI run dependent on paid providers.
what: Set up GitHub Actions for Python/TypeScript checks, builds, migrations, and targeted integration tests.
Make later feature PRs extend the fixture suite as their behavior is implemented.
how: Run formatting/linting, type checks where configured, unit tests, PostgreSQL integration tests, and frontend production build.
Use sanitized fixtures and deterministic time for normalization, deduplication, quote ordering, replay, and notification retry tests.
Start with minimal working gates and extend them in WO-007 through WO-014. Do not wait for all later work to create CI.
Keep external live probes manual/opt-in with explicit budget limits. Never expose provider credentials to untrusted pull requests.
Add a PR checklist describing the issue, behavior, verification evidence, migrations, and known limitations.
done: A clean CI run passes without private keys, provider accounts, or Telegram access.
A deliberate supported-trade regression and a duplicate/replay regression fail the appropriate tests.
Database migrations are exercised on disposable PostgreSQL.
Frontend builds and representative browser flows are checked.
Workflow permissions are minimal and failed checks are not hidden by unconditional success.

title: Expose source health, usage budgets, and retention controls
why: A low-cost personal system must show when its data is stale or its provider/storage usage is growing unexpectedly.
what: Add health/status APIs and a compact dashboard status view.
Track collection lag, recovery gaps, queue age, provider requests/credits where available, and retention jobs.
how: Separate source occurrence-to-ingestion lag from browser RTT and API query time. Record unknown timing rather than manufacturing a latency number.
Show last successful source contact, watched-wallet count, parser errors, oldest queued job, notification failures, and history coverage.
Add monthly usage settings and application-side thresholds for optional backfill/quote work. Do not claim these settings are an absolute vendor spending cap.
Implement bounded deletion/compaction for raw payloads and delivery history; preserve deduplication and declared coverage semantics.
Document baseline server disk/RAM and provider usage from the pilot, plus alerts for stopped collection and a full disk.
done: Disconnecting the source produces a visible stale/degraded state.
Budget thresholds stop or reduce optional work while preserving recorded gaps.
Retention does not break live replay silently; expired cursors request resync.
A small metrics/status page answers whether collection and delivery are healthy.
Storage growth and measured usage are recorded in the pilot report.

title: Prepare private VPS deployment, backups, and rollback
why: The first live release needs an always-on deployment that can restart and recover without exposing a personal control panel.
what: Create a small production Compose deployment for API/frontend, worker, and PostgreSQL.
Document private access, secret provisioning, restart behavior, backup/restore, and version rollback.
how: Use reproducible container builds and explicit image/version tags. Build frontend assets in a build stage and serve them through the application or a small proxy.
Bind the dashboard to loopback/private networking and use an existing trusted tunnel/VPN or SSH forwarding. Do not add a product login system or publish PostgreSQL.
Provision only the selected provider and Telegram credentials on the host; do not place them in GitHub issues, image layers, or logs.
Back up PostgreSQL plus non-secret configuration to an off-machine destination. Write restore and collector-resume steps that preserve delivery state.
Run migrations as a deliberate deployment step. Document schema-compatible rollback and a restore path when a migration cannot be rolled back safely.
done: The documented deployment works on the selected VPS and restarts after a reboot.
An unauthorized public request cannot reach control APIs or the database.
One backup is restored into a separate disposable database and verified.
A restored worker resumes without historical alert flooding.
Release version, deploy procedure, rollback procedure, and expected monthly infrastructure cost are documented.
No new purchase is made merely because it appears in the plan.

title: Validate real traffic and release the first personal beta
why: The first-live milestone should be based on observed operation and correctness, not only a successful build or a screenshot.
what: Run the deployed tool with 10–25 selected wallets and publish a concise acceptance report.
Release a tagged first beta after the launch gate passes; keep unsupported features visibly disabled.
how: Observe at least 24 hours of operation, extending the interval if insufficient representative activity occurs. Record event counts, source coverage, errors, lag, and provider usage.
Verify a sample of supported buys/sells against source transactions. Use recorded fixtures for edge cases not observed during the trial.
Exercise source disconnect, worker restart, browser reconnect, provider throttling, quote outage, duplicate delivery, and backup restore.
Confirm private access and inspect frontend artifacts/logs for accidental credentials. Review notification volume with the user.
Document limitations and remaining defects; do not mark partial-history positions, FOMO metadata, or unsupported routes complete.
done: All first-live dependencies are complete and CI passes.
Feed, history, watch management, details, and Telegram work with real data.
Critical duplicate, missing-event recovery, and transfer-as-buy defects are resolved.
A written acceptance report distinguishes measured results from assumptions.
The repository contains a release tag and a runnable operator guide.
The user can stop/start the host and understand resulting recovery/coverage behavior.

title: Add observed positions and first/add/re-entry/exit semantics
why: Position context makes wallet activity easier to understand, but incomplete history must not produce false first-buy, exit, or P&L claims.
what: Build a per-wallet/token observed quantity ledger with explicit opening-balance provenance and coverage.
Derive first observed buy, add, re-entry, trim, and exit only when available evidence supports them.
how: Choose a reproducible ledger order using chain facts and stable tie-breakers. Preserve adjustments and corrections rather than rewriting unknown history.
Handle transfers, missing opening balances, unsupported routes, token-decimal changes, and partial backfill by downgrading completeness.
Separate observed quantity, current market value, executed amounts, and realized P&L. Do not introduce accounting-grade P&L in this task.
Implement sell-share only when the prior quantity is known; mark unknown instead of dividing by an invented balance.
Rebuild a sample ledger from stored executions and compare it with incremental processing.
done: An unknown opening balance produces partial/unknown position labels.
First buy is labelled first observed unless prior-history completeness is demonstrated.
Transfer-in/out and failed/refunded/corrected events do not masquerade as profitable executions.
Full exit requires supported evidence of the remaining balance.
Incremental and replayed ledgers agree on representative fixtures.
The UI exposes the coverage and estimation method.

title: Implement personal multi-wallet consensus signals
why: Aggregating eligible trades can reduce alert noise and show several watched wallets acting on the same token.
what: Add one versioned configurable signal engine over the personal watch scope.
Support direction, window, minimum participants, amount threshold, exclusions, cooldown, and alert expiry.
how: Define net_usd as eligible confirmed buy USD minus sell USD; define gross-directional metrics separately.
Count distinct wallets unless verified identity links justify person-level aggregation. Store the participating executions and identity basis.
Persist rule versions and signal contributions so late/corrected events can update or invalidate a signal reproducibly.
Specify occurrence-time windows, allowed lateness, insufficient-price behavior, cooldown scope, and maximum notification rate.
Feed signals through the shared canonical live/history and notification paths. Recheck rules for queued delivery and expire stale trading alerts.
done: A fixture with repeated buys from one wallet cannot satisfy a multi-wallet threshold by repetition alone.
A qualifying fixture triggers one signal with inspectable members and totals.
Failed/invalidated executions are excluded and corrections reverse their contributions.
Replay rebuilds signal state without an alert storm.
Token/account filters do not accidentally hide every account-free aggregate signal.
Thresholds are personal settings, not claims of exact Wind algorithm parity.

title: Build local rankings, mover history, and research summaries
why: Stored trade history can show concentration of activity without paying for a separate global ranking product.
what: Add local token heat, unique-buyer/seller boards, directional volumes, net flow, and mover history.
Provide 24h/7d/30d windows only where collection/retention supports them.
how: Write metric definitions with event eligibility, USD-price coverage, window boundaries, and distinct-wallet/person semantics.
Start with indexed SQL and bounded materialized rollups only if measurement requires them; no separate analytics database.
Keep any heat formula transparent and versioned. Do not present a proposed formula as Wind's unpublished score.
Allow drill-down from each score or mover to its source executions and participant list.
For incomplete windows, show partial coverage. Add FOMO-thesis counts only after the thesis adapter exists.
done: Rankings are reproducible from their visible contributing events.
Gross directional volume and net flow cannot be confused.
Missing prices, duplicate identities, and unsupported trades are handled according to the metric contract.
Users can inspect participants and historical windows without unbounded queries.
The interface labels the monitored universe and collection start.

title: Add personal settings, saved views, and configuration portability
why: Personal convenience should not require the account, subscription, and multi-device synchronization systems removed from scope.
what: Provide single-user filter and threshold settings, saved views, pins/ignore with undo, and configuration export/import.
Support useful display preferences without reproducing the commercial workspace.
how: Version the configuration schema and separate server settings from browser-local presentation choices.
Export watches, aliases, groups, settings, and signal definitions; exclude credentials, device secrets, and private source payloads.
Preview imports with duplicate/conflict decisions, validate references, and apply changes transactionally where practical.
Implement saved account/group/chain filters and bounded pin/ignore state. Preserve reading continuity across view changes.
Treat drag/resize layouts and additional language/theme variants as optional follow-up refinements; do not block the personal acceptance gate on them.
done: A configuration export/import round-trip preserves non-secret settings.
Exports contain no bot token, provider key, or infrastructure credential.
Invalid imports report specific errors without corrupting the existing configuration.
Saved views use the same backend filter semantics as the feed.
Ignore has an undo path and pins have an explicit retention policy.
No login, cross-user settings merge, or membership logic is introduced.

title: Qualify FOMO identity, thesis, clan, and order data access
why: FOMO-specific behavior cannot be reconstructed solely from blockchain transactions. This gate prevents fake identity mappings or nonfunctional feature promises.
what: Identify a documented/authorized acquisition path for each needed FOMO capability.
Produce a capability matrix and go/no-go decision before enabling dependent adapters.
how: Evaluate stable user IDs, wallet mappings, thesis IDs/text/token mentions, clan membership/size, and off-chain order state as separate capabilities.
Record source provenance, permission requirements, rate limits, historical coverage, monthly costs, replay/edit semantics, and representative sanitized payloads.
Verify an identity link against explicit source evidence; a similar name or shared funding is not enough.
Document unsupported data as blocked. Keep manual wallet labels and wallet-only monitoring available.
Do not scrape private endpoints without access, bypass sign-in, reuse Wind's backend, or assume a trading SDK exposes social metadata.
done: Each capability is marked verified, partial, unavailable, or unresolved with evidence.
Pricing and access requirements are recorded or explicitly unknown.
A viable source has representative fixtures and a recovery strategy.
Dependent issues specify which verified capabilities they require.
If no source is available, the blocked state is documented and the wallet-only release remains usable.

title: Integrate verified FOMO identities and token theses
why: FOMO account and thesis context is valuable only when source identities and token references remain attributable and up to date.
what: Implement the verified identity and thesis capabilities from the source qualification gate.
Extend profile/token/search views with FOMO-specific evidence, without restoring excluded social platforms.
how: Use immutable source user IDs, mutable aliases, and evidence-bearing wallet links. Keep manual labels distinguishable from source-confirmed identity.
Persist thesis IDs, text, edits/deletions where supported, token mentions, timestamps, and provenance.
Validate token mentions by chain/address. Distinguish commentary from an actual buy; do not infer a purchase from a thesis.
Process thesis revisions through canonical updates and source checkpoint recovery. Use bounded retention and a stated collection start.
Show grouped author commentary and optional on-demand cached translation only after its provider and budget are explicitly configured.
done: Account rename preserves history and correct wallet links.
Two similar names never merge without evidence.
Theses appear on the appropriate token/profile pages with source/time labels.
A thesis without an execution cannot create a buy or position.
Unsupported edits/deletions and historical gaps are declared.
If source access is absent, the feature remains disabled and this issue is blocked rather than falsely completed.

title: Reconcile FOMO order attempts with on-chain executions
why: Preview, pending, refund, failure, and revocation describe source order state; they are not interchangeable with blockchain confirmation.
what: Implement a source-evidenced order lifecycle only for capabilities proved in WO-023.
Link orders and execution legs conservatively, preserving uncertain matches and corrections.
how: Keep off-chain order status and chain confirmation in separate fields and state machines.
Match by stable source order ID or transaction references. Use explicit confidence/evidence for weaker associations; never merge solely on similar time/amount.
Handle partial fills, refunds, revocations, and source corrections with reversible contributions to positions and signals.
Display attempted orders distinctly and make failed attempts ineligible for confirmed volume/consensus.
For multi-chain orders, retain separate legs until the selected chain adapters can establish the final economic outcome.
done: Fixtures cover successful, failed, refunded, revoked, unmatched, and duplicate order updates where the source supports them.
A failed attempt that never reached the chain is shown only from an actual upstream record.
Execution finality does not automatically imply the intended off-chain order succeeded.
Corrections update existing cards and derived totals rather than adding duplicate economic events.
Unavailable lifecycle states stay disabled or unknown.

title: Implement clan membership snapshots and resonance
why: Clan participation is meaningful only with a known membership denominator and historical membership context.
what: Persist source-backed clan membership snapshots and calculate versioned participation signals.
Expose monitored-member coverage separately from authoritative clan size.
how: Gate the feature on qualified membership and effective-time data; otherwise use clearly labelled personal watch groups.
Choose written participation/window/amount/tier rules and record the membership snapshot used for each calculation.
Deduplicate identities with evidence, use eligible executions, and apply the same corrections/cooldowns/expiry mechanisms as other signals.
Show the actual participating members, total authoritative members where available, and number of monitored members.
Deliver through the existing feed/Telegram path; no independent audio or wake system.
done: A membership change produces a new effective snapshot rather than silently rewriting old denominators.
Monitored subset size is never presented as total clan size.
Signal participants and thresholds are inspectable and reproducible.
Missing membership data disables the ratio-based signal with a clear reason.
Duplicate/corrected trades do not inflate participation.

title: Extend to selected additional chains through qualified adapters
why: Multi-chain support should reuse the product model while acknowledging that receipts, routes, confirmation, and provider coverage differ by network.
what: Select the next genuinely needed network and document a per-chain capability/cost decision.
Implement and validate adapters one chain at a time rather than enabling every chain label seen in Wind.
how: For each candidate, verify network ID, environment, official RPC/indexer source, transaction decoding, history, quote coverage, and usage cost. Create a chain-specific checklist before coding.
Implement the shared adapter contract using receipts/logs or qualified decoded transactions; define token identity, address normalization, finality, and reorg behavior.
Reuse recovery, canonical revisions, filters, notification rules, and exact chain/address search.
Treat bridge transfers and cross-chain order legs explicitly; do not turn every bridge receipt into a purchase.
Keep unsupported networks behind disabled capabilities. Record actual coverage instead of claiming generic EVM support automatically works everywhere.
done: Each enabled network has a published capability matrix and representative real/sanitized fixtures.
Same-address tokens on different chains remain distinct.
Reorg/failure/correction and restart recovery scenarios behave correctly.
Trade attribution and market values are verified against the chosen chain source.
Cost and latency are measured before increasing the watch universe.
Networks without a qualified source remain out of the enabled configuration.

title: Verify the expanded personal release and complete the operator guide
why: The expanded release should have an honest feature/capability report and remain maintainable by one person.
what: Run a final acceptance pass over all enabled personal features and publish a release/runbook update.
Resolve or explicitly defer source-blocked capabilities without pretending they shipped.
how: Review every retained feature against the scope checklist; distinguish implemented, source-blocked, deliberately deferred, and excluded features.
Re-run meaningful correctness, correction, replay, notification, restore, and private-access checks across enabled adapters.
Measure 25–100 watched accounts only if actual usage justifies expansion; record provider costs, storage growth, lag, query performance, and gaps.
Document routine provider-key rotation, stopped-host recovery, data retention, backup restore, and monthly usage review.
Tag the release and link all completed issues and known limitations. No arbitrary algorithm is called an exact Wind reproduction.
done: All enabled features have source-backed behavior and recorded validation evidence.
Each unavailable FOMO/chain capability has an explicit documented decision; blocked issues are not marked implemented.
Recovery and restore are tested with the enabled feature set.
README and runbook commands match the actual application.
The actual recurring cost is recorded separately from the initial estimate.
A single operator can deploy, inspect, recover, and maintain the tool.
